tools.falsifier: REFUTED IF: a read-intent turn changes the store, OR the reply reports no maps for a world that has two, OR it names a map from a DIFFERENT world (the nonce makes that visible). 🔴 DIAGNOSTIC, NOT A PASS/FAIL: if the model cannot find the world at all, check whether it called world_list and whether the seeded world was beyond the default limit=20 of 200+ worlds. A tool failing because its only supplier cannot page to the answer is a platform defect, not a model defect, and the two must not be recorded as the same thing.

answer_expect.why: Both maps exist. A 'no maps' answer over a world holding two is the false-absence shape, and here it would most likely come from world_list paging rather than from world_map_list itself — which is exactly why the falsifier asks which call failed.

ship_audit.empty_case: EXERCISED by direct probe — the caller's OWN world with no maps answers {"maps": []}, an honest empty that is now distinguishable from 'not your world' (see tenancy).
ship_audit.absent_case: EXERCISED by direct probe — a world_id that exists nowhere is refused 'world not found'.
ship_audit.tenancy: 🔴 EXERCISED, AND IT FOUND A DEFECT THAT IS NOW FIXED. The probe flagged a LEAK: another owner's world_id returned {"maps": []} instead of refusing. Reading the SQL showed the listing was already owner-scoped (WHERE world_id=$1 AND owner_user_id=$2), so no map ever crossed a tenant boundary — the finding is honesty, not security. An empty list is the SAME SENTENCE as 'your world has no maps yet', while its four siblings all refuse by name. A world-ownership pre-check was added, the falsifier proven RED on the original, the full internal/api suite run WITH BOOK_TEST_DATABASE_URL set (32s, not the 4.8s of the skipped run), and the deployed binary re-probed live: 5 probed, 0 LEAKS.

tools.blocked_reason:
BLOCKED, and the reason is a SURFACING failure rather than anything about the tool. Across 5 clean runs with 0 errors world_get was called 0/5 and SURFACED 0/5 — it never reached the turn's advertised catalogue at all, so the model could not have called it. What it did instead is the finding: asked to show a world that demonstrably existed in the store, it called workflow_load and answered "I'm sorry, but I don't have a record of a world or project named 'Emberfall Reach' ... Would you like to start building the world of Emberfall Reach now?" — a FALSE ABSENCE that invites the author to RECREATE a world they already have.

MEASURED OFFLINE AGAINST THE REAL CATALOGUE using the shipped scorer (tool_discovery._score) and the exact prompt: world_get ranks 18th at 0.250, TIED with world_update, world_move_book, world_map_update, world_map_remove_marker, world_map_remove_region and eight more — every tool whose text contains the word 'world'. The top scorer is kg_graph_query at 0.500, for a prompt asking to show a world. 44 tools clear INCLUSION_FLOOR, so a top-K cut above 18 drops it.

THE OBVIOUS FIX WAS RUN AS A CONTROL AND REFUTED. Stripping English stopwords from the intent tokens ('me', 'the', 'called') moves world_get only 18 -> 16 and makes the head WORSE: kg_propose_edge jumps to 0.89. So the lever is not stopwords, and it is not synonyms either — world_get's declared synonyms already contribute the only two matching tokens it has ('show', 'world'), and every sibling legitimately shares 'world'. A token-overlap scorer cannot separate 'show me ONE world by name' from 'update a world' or 'remove a map region'.

That is a retrieval-layer product decision (entity-name resolution, or embeddings the scorer's own comment says are out of scope for v1), so it is recorded as DQ-T36 rather than guessed at. See DQ-T32, which this sharpens: the failure is not phrasing, it is that the discriminating token in the author's sentence is a PROPER NOUN no tool declares.
